item.title: 2002 AlumKnight Christine Igisomar to lead MCS in 2026
item.description: (MCS) — The Board of Directors of Mount Carmel School has named 2002 AlumKnight Christine Torres Igisomar as the incoming President of the school. Upon retiring after 24 years of active duty military service, she will take the helm of leadership at the beginning of the 2026-2027 school year in August. The post 2002 AlumKnight Christine Igisomar to lead MCS in 2026 appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Tinian Hot Pepper Festival on Feb. 13-14
item.description: (MVA) — The iconic Tinian Hot Pepper Festival returns to the Marianas for its 22nd staging on Feb. 13-14, 2026, bringing two days of food, fun, and flaming-hot island flavor to a Pacific island steeped in history. item.title: FAC remains the same for January
item.description: (CUC) — The Commonwealth Utilities Corporation announces that the Fuel Adjustment Charge or FAC remains the same at $0.19706 per kWh for the month of January. The post FAC remains the same for January appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: Woman injured in fall during bird count on Rota
item.description: A WOMAN conducting a bird count with a biologist on Rota last week fell off a cliff and was later medevaced to Guam for treatment, Variety learned. The post Woman injured in fall during bird count on Rota appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: CUC board clears path for AP Energy appeal, shuts down other protests
item.description: THE Commonwealth Utilities Corp. board on Thursday, Jan. 8 voted to advance an appeal filed by AP Energy LLC over its disqualification from a major solar-and-battery procurement for Saipan, Tinian and Rota, while unanimously rejecting a separate protest by PKM Summit Ridge and declining to revisit a request from Tang’s Corporation. item.title: Former government prosecutor granted CNMI law license
item.description: FORMER head of the CNMI government’s anti-corruption task force James Robert Kingman has been sworn in as a practicing attorney in the Commonwealth and is preparing to open a private law practice after passing the CNMI Bar exam in July. The post Former government prosecutor granted CNMI law license appeared first on Marianas Variety News & Views.

item.title: $7.1M Naftan road project opens to public
item.description: GOVERNOR David M. Apatang, Department of Public Works Secretary Ray N. Yumul, Speaker Edmund S. Villagomez, Rep. Roman C. Benavente, and Commonwealth Ports Authority officials on Thursday held a ribbon-cutting ceremony to open the newly improved Naftan Road, also known as Route 301, and a portion of Flame Tree Road, or Route 304. item.title: Regarding the FY 2025 fiscal report
item.description: FOR the past few years, the administration’s annual fiscal report has read like 80% press release and only 20% useful information. The latest report is quite an improvement. It’s still a multi-page pat-on-the-back, but it now includes more pertinent details, some of which can be considered key data and not just wishful thinking dressed up as statistics.
